correctness.rationale: Each unary type is an admissible ideal–filter pair. Keeping the two distinct new points incomparable, the only potential new failures of strict transitivity are the paths through an old point in one of the two opposing cross intersections. Their simultaneous nonemptiness, for individually admissible types, would force both u<l and l<u. Thus the product of cross-disjointness indicators is also their sum minus one. This makes every proposed four-term mixed vector radical, and their coefficient-one mixed pivots make the replacement unimodular. Subtracting the neutral vector from each pure vector leaves the cross block -Q and neutral norm 1. On complementing filters, subtracting the full-ideal row and expanding along the empty-ideal column identifies det Q up to sign with the zeta determinant on nonempty proper ideals, which is 1 in an inclusion-compatible order. Multiplying the second pure basis by the inverse cross block then gives the asserted integral hyperbolic planes. This proves the full radical basis, Smith form, rank over all fields and real inertia, including the empty-base matrix [1]. The included script and its output were inspected, not executed; its helper checks the zeta triangular pattern rather than computing det Q numerically, and the finite tests do not prove the all-base claim.
residual_risks: This is the feasibility matrix for distinct nonalgebraic realizations; it is not the ordinary incomparability matrix of the finite base, nor a count of all ordered two-point types.
